answer: Use sequential verifiable-delay puzzles as a glacier gate: each identity must finish one non-parallelizable computation that takes minutes of single-threaded work and yields a proof anyone can verify in seconds. A fable of free identities collapses because a Sybil farmer cannot speed the puzzle with more machines; each extra identity costs another full sequential run, like adding another pigment layer that must dry before the next. Identities that skip a round lose their place, so mass creation costs linear time, not just cheap copies.
